newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat oil ends up, touches post-Gulf War high.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat oil ends up, touches post-Gulf War high.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil touched its post-Gulf War high and ended Wednesday sharply higher after historically low heating oil stocks showed a meager build in the latest weekly oil inventory data, traders said.
"Pretty much the major factor was the APIs. The stocks are perceived as really low, and the build was lower than expected," said Gerald Samuels, managing director of ARB Oil.

October heating oil ended the day 2.08 cents higher at 71.77 cents a gallon after rising to 72.25 cents, heating oil's post-Gulf War high hit the week of November 8, 1991. Strong technical buying also contributed to the rally.
"After heating oil broke 70.15 and 70.20, it was just off to the races," said Victor Yu, vice president of Refco Energy Group, citing resistance levels that were broken.
Heating oil pushed up November crude oil which settled 39
cents higher at $24.46 a barrel. October gasoline closed up 0.27 cent to 63.10 cents a gallon.

On Tuesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said distillate stocks, of which heating oil is a component, rose a mere 303,000 barrels. Traders were expecting an increase near two million barrels, a seasonal build in preparation for the winter.

Heating oil stocks are 18 million barrels below year ago levels, with most of the deficit in the northeastern United States, the world's largest market for heating oil. Heating oil's firm backwardation is discouraging storage build due to the higher price of the spot month, traders said.

For the week ended September 20, gasoline stocks showed a larger-than-build with demand slackening due to the end of the peak summer driving season. Still, gasoline prices were supported by the rally in heating oil, traders said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
